content.value_statement: API teams lose time when contracts are unclear or written after implementation. This skill guides OpenAPI-first design, TypeScript generation, validation, documentation, and mock workflows.
actual_capabilities: Drafts OpenAPI 3.1 paths, schemas, responses, and security definitions.
Shows folder structures for split API specifications and reusable references.
Explains TypeScript type generation with openapi-typescript.
Shows type-safe client setup with openapi-fetch and Orval.
Outlines request validation with Zod-based schemas.
Describes Swagger UI, Scalar, and Prism mock server workflows.
limitations: Does not execute generators or install packages by itself.
Generated examples still require project-specific review and testing.
Complex domain models may need manual schema refinement.
Runtime security controls must be implemented in the application.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product API
use_cases.description: Define endpoints, data models, error responses, and client types before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Document an Existing REST Service
use_cases.description: Convert current behavior into an OpenAPI contract that teams can review and maintain.

use_cases.title: Standardize Service Contracts
use_cases.description: Create consistent patterns for pagination, errors, versioning, validation, and generated SDKs across services.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an OpenAPI 3.1 contract for a todo API. Include CRUD endpoints, request schemas, responses, and common errors.

prompt_templates.title: Add Type Generation
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this API contract with reusable schemas and operation IDs. Explain how to generate TypeScript types and validate requests.

prompt_templates.title: Design Team Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a schema-first workflow for frontend and backend teams. Include mock server use, reviews, versioning, and documentation publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Large Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this OpenAPI contract for maintainability, breaking changes, duplicated schemas, weak validation, and code generation risks. Suggest prioritized improvements.

output_examples.input: A team needs a user management API before backend work starts.
output: OpenAPI contract outline with user, authentication, pagination, and error sections.
Review checklist for frontend and backend teams.
Type generation plan for shared client models.

output_examples.input: A legacy service lacks typed clients.
output_examples.output: A migration plan that maps endpoints to OpenAPI operations, then generates TypeScript types and a client.

output_examples.input: Frontend development is blocked by missing backend endpoints.
output_examples.output: A mock server workflow using the contract, shared examples, and review steps for API changes.

best_practices: Agree on operation IDs, response shapes, and error models before implementation starts.
Keep large contracts modular with reusable schemas, responses, and path references.
Review API contracts like production code before generating clients or SDKs.
anti_patterns: Do not mix schema-first and code-first sources without a clear ownership rule.
Do not hide breaking changes behind version labels without migration notes.
Do not generate clients from unreviewed contracts or stale specifications.

faq.question: Does this skill run OpenAPI tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains commands and patterns, but tool execution needs explicit user action.

faq.question: Which OpenAPI version does it target?
faq.answer: It focuses on OpenAPI 3.1, while many patterns also apply to OpenAPI 3.0.

faq.question: Can it help with existing APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help describe current endpoints as a contract for review and documentation.

faq.question: Does it replace backend validation?
faq.answer: No. It outlines validation patterns, but applications must enforce validation at runtime.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it useful for generated clients?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains operation IDs, reusable schemas, and generation workflows for typed clients.
